name: ovarian-interventional-trial-landscape-v2
normalization: Unicode NFKC, casefold, Greek alpha α to 'alpha', Unicode dash punctuation and ASCII '-' to spaces, collapse Unicode whitespace. Unicode word-boundary literal phrases, independently within each field or list item. No stemming, negation removal, or inference that a mention is an eligibility rule or an outcome.
phase_rule: One study in its canonical combined-phase category. NA is distinct from an absent phase list. Reject unknown, duplicate, or NA mixed with another phase.
intervention_rule: Count a study once in each distinct intervention type string on its intervention list. An empty or absent list is NOT_REPORTED and is not also counted under a type. A list that has types is not also NOT_REPORTED. These are study-level presence counts, so the type columns overlap and need not sum to the cohort.
status_rule: One overallStatus value per study. The status counts sum to the cohort. This is the status field on the retrieved record, not a reconstructed history.
fralpha_adc_rule: Count fralpha_adc when any fralpha_adc_names term matches, or when any folr1_language term and any fralpha_adc_context term both match. Context terms alone do not count. This is name and phrase presence for the agent in the repository FDA notice (mirvetuximab soravtansine) plus a folate-receptor ADC phrase. It is not a complete ADC catalogue and not evidence of benefit.
ca125_rule: ca125_language is marker phrasing. It is not counted as an MUC16-directed target class.
language_buckets_note: biomarker_generic, brca, hrd, platinum_resistant and platinum_refractory repeat the 2026-11-05 dictionary on this field set only. Eligibility text is not searched and the cohort is not limited to recruiting studies, so these counts are not a replay of that snapshot.
searched_fields_note: Titles, brief summary, condition list, keyword list, and intervention names. Eligibility criteria were not requested and are not archived.
efficacy: Outcome, results, and adverse-event fields were not requested. Class counts are registrations whose text matched a lexicon. They are not response rates, not survival, and not a treatment recommendation.
interpretation: Public registry metadata only. A keyword hit can be a negation, an exclusion, a background sentence, or a basket trial. No eligibility inference, ranking, or clinical guidance.
